text:
Samira: FYI customer acme-media reporting a sudden spike of 429s from their Dedicated pool eu-west-1-pool-03 starting ~09:40 UTC. They say it affects both generation and embedding endpoints.
Diego: Can you paste a sample request/response headers or rate-limit headers from the tenant?
Samira: Pasting header from their error:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rw-units-remaining: 0
x-rw-units-limit: 120
x-rw-units-reset: 167
x-rw-token-remaining: 0
x-rw-token-limit: 60000
```
They also sent this snippet of their quota object from our UI (screenshot converted): `quota_type: units_per_minute` but they expected tokens_per_minute.
Alex: That mismatch rings a bell — we recently changed default quota schema to favor token-based limits but our tenant migration job had a fallback that could accidentally write the wrong unit for some older dedicated tenants.
Priya: Customer insists they didn't change anything on their end and only saw the regression after today's deployment window. They're asking for temporary un-throttled access while we investigate.
Diego: If it's the migration bug, we can flip their quota back to tokens-per-minute quickly. Need an explicit runbook: tenant id, pool id, and desired tokens/min value.
Samira: Tenant id: tenant-7284, pool: eu-west-1-pool-03. They want us to set tokens_per_minute = 120000 as temporary.
Alex: I'll check audit logs and the migration job runs between 03:00-03:10 UTC. If the quota was written as units_per_minute with a low value it explains the aggressive 429s because our serving runtime evaluates units first and falls back to lower cap.
ops-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-2247 - Dedicated tenant throttling; assignees Diego, Alex.
Diego: Quick mitigation plan:
1) Apply emergency override via admin API: `POST /admin/tenants/tenant-7284/override` with `{quota_type: "tokens_per_minute", value: "120000"}` (this will bypass migration artifact)
2) Monitor pool util + X-Rate-Limit headers for 15m
3) Roll permanent fix to migration job and backfill any affected tenants
Samira: I'll request the emergency override and ping legal/CS for approval. Customer asked for timeframe ~30m.
Alex: I pulled audit: migration-job-2026-03-17 wrote quota_type=units_per_minute for tenant-7284 at 03:05:12 UTC, value=200. That explains the 0 remaining units within minutes for their traffic pattern.
Priya: I'll tell the customer we're applying an override and will follow up when throttles stop.
Diego: After override we'll also enable temporary per-tenant burst window to let queued requests through: `admin.enable_burst(tenant_id="tenant-7284", seconds=120)`
Samira: Doing override now, will report back once X-Rate-Limit headers show increased limits. :crossed_fingers:
Samira: Update 09:58 UTC — override applied, headers now show `x-rw-units-limit: 120000`, 429s dropped. Customer confirms improved latency.
Alex: I'll open a follow-up PR to add a migration validation step that rejects writing units_per_minute for tenants that previously had token-based quotas and add a backfill to convert suspicious entries.
Diego: Leaving this oncall handoff to Alex for the permanent fix. I'll monitor for 1h and then clear the incident.
Priya: Customer extremely relieved, asked for a short postmortem and confirmation when migration fix is live.
Samira: Noted — will draft a short postmortem and include the audit timeline + mitigation steps.
ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-2247 updated: status -> monitoring.
